guideTitle: 6 Best Door Knob Grips Under $20 in 2026
metaTitle: Best Door Knob Grips Under $20 in 2026
metaDescription: Six budget door knob covers compared, from a six-piece Eggone ribbed grip set and Enjoy Cover two-packs to HLARTNET cushion covers for temperature.
introParagraphs: The top of this budget range adds one product that changes what a door knob cover is for. The HLARTNET six-piece set is described as an anti-scald and antifreeze cushion, so it is aimed at a knob that is hot or cold to touch rather than a hand that struggles to grip. Everything else in the lineup is a silicone grip sleeve. That split gives you two real decisions: grip help versus temperature cushioning, and how many doors you need to cover.

We evaluated six distinct listings: the HLARTNET six-piece round handle cushion cover, the Eggone six-piece ribbed silicone grips, the Enjoy Cover two-pack, the Enjoy Cover upgraded ergonomic two-pack, the Able Life EZ Doorknob Grips and the Enjoy Cover single-pack doorstop grip. Judgments rest on listed dimensions, materials, pack counts and extras. We make no medical claims about any of these. Where a listing gives no figure for fit or pack contents, we say to check the product page rather than guess.

At this cap you give up nothing that a lower cap offered, but you do not get a lever handle either. A cover only changes the surface and thickness of the knob. For a hand that cannot close around a round shape, a lever replacement is the only real fix, and a cover is the cheap first try.

products.name: Eggone 6 Pcs Silicone Door Knob Grips
products.description:
Eggone is a six-piece set of silicone grips, each listed at 3 inches wide and 2 inches deep, with a ribbed texture and glow inserts. The listing says the covers make awkward round knobs easier to turn and give a better grip for weaker or older hands. It describes the material as chemically stable, durable silica gel, and says the ribbed texture is comfortable on older fingers.

The ribbing is the feature that does the grip work, giving fingertips something to push against that a smooth sleeve cannot. A single stated size is both a help and a limit, because a knob outside the 3 by 2 inch range may not take it. The glow insert is a small extra, though the listing does not say how bright it is. It has no doorstop bumper.

Six covers cover a typical home, and spares are included if one loosens over time. Next to the Enjoy Cover two-pack, the Eggone gives three times the count for a household. Against the HLARTNET six-pack, it is built for grip rather than temperature. It is the strongest all-round choice here. Because the pack is six, you can fit the hallway, bathroom and bedroom knobs and still have spares for the next stretch-out. That count is the main reason it edges ahead of the HLARTNET, which also gives six but solves a different problem.
products.bestFor: Whole-home coverage with a ribbed, textured grip.
pros: Six pieces cover most interior doors
Glow inserts help in dim hallways
Stated 3 x 2 in size makes fit checkable
cons: Single stated size may not fit big knobs

products.name: HLARTNET 6PCS Round Door Handle Cover

specList.label: Purpose
specList.value: Cushion against hot and cold metal

products.description:
HLARTNET sells six round door handle covers, each 2.8 inches high with a 2.6 inch inner diameter. The listing calls them anti-scald in summer and antifreeze in winter, so the aim is to stop a metal knob from burning or chilling your hand. It lists use on front doors, living room doors and others, and says six pieces covers daily use and replacements.

This is a cushion cover rather than a dedicated grip sleeve, so it will not match a ribbed sleeve for friction. The listing tells you to measure your handle before buying, and the 2.6 inch inner diameter is the number to check. It is the one pick here suited to an exposed outdoor knob in strong sun or freezing weather.

Set-up is a slip-over, and the six-piece count gives spares. Compared with the Eggone at 3 by 2 inches and ribbed texture, the HLARTNET trades friction for thermal comfort. Choose it when temperature, not grip, is your problem. If your front door knob sits in direct sun, a cushion cover like this makes the first touch more comfortable. If your complaint is a smooth knob that slips, this is the wrong pick.
products.bestFor: Exposed knobs that get hot in summer or icy in winter.
pros: Cushions against hot and cold metal
Stated 2.6 in inner diameter to check
cons: Less grip than a ribbed sleeve
Thermal claim is the maker's, check the product page

products.name: Enjoy Cover 2 Pack Upgraded Ergonomic Door Knob Grips
products.description:
The upgraded two-pack from Enjoy Cover is soft non-slip silicone with an ergonomic shape. It is listed as compatible with most standard round knobs, stretching to accommodate different sizes while keeping a secure fit. Installation is a simple stretch and slip with no tools or modification.

The upgraded label is not explained in the highlights, so check the page for what changed. Two covers is a small count next to the six-piece sets. It has no bumper.

Compared with the standard two-pack, it is the newer design from the same maker. Next to the Eggone, it offers a branded ergonomic shape for two doors. It is a tidy pick for a small home. It makes the most sense for a flat with two round knobs that matter, such as the bathroom and the bedroom.
products.bestFor: Two doors where you want a branded ergonomic shape.

products.name: Enjoy Cover 2 Pack Silicone Door Knob Grips
products.description:
The standard Enjoy Cover two-pack is 100 percent silicone, described as non-toxic, BPA free and allergy free. The listing says one size fits most standard knobs, installs in seconds and washes with soap and water. It is the simplest and most washable pair in the lineup.

There is no bumper, and two covers is a small count. The listing says it meets all safety standards, which is a general claim to verify. It is a plain sleeve.

Compared with the upgraded pack, it is the standard version. Against the Able Life, it gives more stated detail. For a small home that wants simple, washable covers, it is a safe default. It also gives you a clean pair to wash and swap, which the six-piece sets do less neatly.
products.bestFor: A simple, washable pair for two doors.
pros: Non-toxic, BPA free per the listing

products.name: Enjoy Cover Doorstop Door Handle Grip, Single Pack
products.description:
Enjoy Cover sells this one as a single all-in-one cover: a grip sleeve for the knob plus a soft bumper that keeps the knob from striking the wall. Per the listing, it pairs a non-slip grip with wall protection in an ergonomic shape. One pack handles one door, so it suits a single problem doorway rather than a whole hallway.

The bumper adds bulk on one side. Sold singly, it needs a purchase per door. It is the only doorstop-style cover in this lineup.

Against the Eggone, it offers a bumper that the Eggone lacks. If one wall keeps getting hit, it is the focused fix. The price of that focus is bulk on one side and a purchase per door.
products.bestFor: One door that keeps hitting the wall.

products.name: Able Life EZ Doorknob Grips
products.description:
Able Life offers non-slip silicone covers that stretch over a knob, listed as a knob turner and handle gripper. The listing says it opens doors easily, costs less than a lever replacement and installs easily. It is a different brand from the others.

The listing gives few details, so check size and pack. There is no bumper. It is a plain sleeve.

It installs by stretching, with no tools. Compared with the Eggone, it is thinner on detail. It is worth considering if you prefer a different brand. Its sparse listing is a reason to read questions on the page before buying.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a plain sleeve from a third brand.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Decide what problem the knob really has before comparing sets. The Eggone, Enjoy Cover and Able Life listings are grip sleeves, while the HLARTNET is described as a cushion cover that is anti-scald in summer and antifreeze in winter. A ribbed sleeve will not do much for a knob that burns your palm in July, and a cushion will not add friction to a slippery handle. Match the product to the actual complaint rather than to the highest pack count. If both problems apply, start with the Eggone for grip and add the HLARTNET only on the exposed door.

Measure your knob before ordering, because size is the most common reason these covers fail. The Eggone lists 3 inches wide by 2 inches deep, the HLARTNET 2.8 inches high with a 2.6 inch inner diameter, and the Enjoy Cover listings say most standard round knobs. A cover that is too small will not go on, and one that is too large will spin without turning the latch. Write the knob diameter and depth down and compare against the page. The HLARTNET listing itself tells you to measure the handle first.

Texture is the cheapest grip upgrade you can buy at this cap. The Eggone has a ribbed surface that its listing calls comfortable for older fingers, while the Enjoy Cover covers use soft non-slip silicone without ribbing. Ribs help most with damp or lotioned hands where smooth silicone starts to slide. Choose ribs if your fingers skate across a smooth sleeve, and smooth if you prefer a slimmer feel. Wipe any cover now and then, since dust and hand cream both reduce friction.

Pack count decides how many doors you cover per order. The Eggone and HLARTNET each give six pieces, the Enjoy Cover two-packs give two, and the single doorstop gives one. Count the knobs you use every day, which is typically bathroom, bedroom and entry. Six covers is usually enough for one household with a spare or two. Buying singles for every door gets expensive and leaves you with mismatched sleeves.

A bumper protects the wall at the cost of bulk on one side, and only the single Enjoy Cover pack here includes one. It makes sense for a door that is often thrown open against plaster, such as a child room or a bathroom beside a hallway. For a door that swings freely into open space, the bumper adds thickness without any benefit. Check which direction your door swings before ordering. A plain sleeve is slimmer and easier to grip.

A cover does not change the shape of the handle, and that is the most important limit to understand. The Able Life listing itself says its grips cost less than a lever replacement, which is an honest statement of the trade. A lever needs less hand closure and can be pushed with a wrist, which no knob cover can match. Add-on lever extensions can stress a latch, so fit them carefully. If a cover does not solve your problem, the next step is a lever, not a thicker cover.

howWeEvaluated.description: We separated grip sleeves from the HLARTNET temperature cushion. The Eggone leads for grip with a ribbed surface, while the HLARTNET leads for hot and cold knobs. Based on product specs. The Enjoy Cover listings focus on ergonomics and non-slip silicone, which sits between the two extremes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stated sizes
howWeEvaluated.description: The Eggone gives 3 by 2 inches, the HLARTNET 2.8 inches high with a 2.6 inch inner diameter. The others say standard round knobs. Where a listing gave no figure, we treated fit as unconfirmed.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pack coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: The Eggone and HLARTNET give six pieces. The Enjoy Cover two-packs give two, and the doorstop one. The Eggone and HLARTNET lead at six, so they offer the lowest cost per door.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted the Eggone glow insert and the Enjoy Cover doorstop bumper as the notable extras. Neither extra is independently measured, so we describe them only as the maker does.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use and care
howWeEvaluated.description: All slip or stretch on without tools. The Enjoy Cover two-pack lists washing with soap and water. Removal is the reverse of stretching on, with no adhesive involved.

faq.a: The Eggone six-piece set, because it combines ribbed grip with whole-home coverage. The listing states 3 by 2 inches, so check fit against your knob first. The Enjoy Cover two-packs cover fewer doors but have more detail on washing and materials. Pick them if you only have two doors to cover.

It is a cushion cover for knobs that get too hot or too cold to touch comfortably. The listing describes it as anti-scald in summer and antifreeze in winter, with a 2.6 inch inner diameter and 2.8 inch height. It does not add much friction, so it is not a replacement for a ribbed grip. Treat the thermal claim as the maker's and check the product page.

No, and fit is the usual reason these fail. Sizes vary by listing: the Eggone is 3 by 2 inches and the HLARTNET has a 2.6 inch inner diameter. The Enjoy Cover covers say most standard round knobs. Measure the knob before ordering and compare with the page.

faq.q: Can a cover replace a lever handle?
faq.a: No, and this is a common misconception. A cover adds surface and friction but keeps the round shape. A lever needs less hand closure and can be pushed with a wrist or elbow. If a cover does not solve it, move to a lever.
Only the single-pack Enjoy Cover doorstop grip in this lineup. The soft bumper stops the knob hitting the wall. It adds bulk on one side. Skip it for a door that swings freely.
The Enjoy Cover two-pack says soap and water, and silicone wipes clean. A damp cloth is enough for most dirt. Avoid harsh solvents on silicone. Check the product page for the other covers.

faq.q: Are these safe around children or pets?
faq.a: The Enjoy Cover two-pack describes non-toxic, BPA free silicone and the Eggone calls its material chemically stable. A sleeve is not a childproofing device, since it makes a knob easier to turn. Small removable pieces like glow inserts deserve a check on the page if toddlers are around. Replace a cover that cracks or tears.

faq.q: Can I use a grip cover and a cushion cover together?
faq.a: Not sensibly, because both are sized to slide directly onto the knob and stacking them would make the stack too thick to turn. Pick the one that matches your main complaint, grip or temperature. On a front door that is both icy and slippery, the Eggone for friction is the better first try, since a ribbed surface also insulates a little from the metal beneath. Check the product pages for any maker guidance on combining covers.
